Autosurfing
I have been autosurfing for about 10 months now and am completely hooked. The general idea, for those who dont know is that you sign up for a program you feel good about (see below). You then pay an amount of money you feel comfortable spending into the program (or surf on any free units the site may give). In return you view other members websites in an "autosurf" window in order to make cash. After viewing a set amount of sites, you are paid a percentage of your membership level. You make money because your upgrade will be active long enough for you to make all your money back, and then begin to profit. You can also compound your earnings and earn even more.

I've earned some and lost some (profit = approx $25,000 CDN, minus about $8000 stolen by stormpay recently), but I've generrally come out ahead. This is the program I'm currently using - which is paying.

The NEW Eprofit Works - This is a combination of Autosurf-biz as well as the old eprofit surf. If you are currently a member of either your accounts have been combined. They will pay to their own brand new payment processor (which will then pay to egold and other options), so we need not worry about 3rd parties pulling the same garbage we experienced lately with Stormpay.Dan and Colleen are considered (among others) the top admins in the business. They are honest and have been paying out consitently since both programs started. Paying

UPDATE - Eprofit works no longer pays by percentage, but by bonuses given while surfing. I just made $60 my first session.

So this is one program i am with that has stayed strong thorugh the recent hard times. I have faith they will stay strong, because they have already been through everything without a scratch.

Dadndaves will also go strong again in the near future, but for now are not taking members.

I know we're all a bit jaded after the stormpay fiasco that ended our beloved 12dp (I lost $8000 in that mess), but fuck it. I love doing this, and so long as there are honest programs this remains a good income subsidy.

So post what new programs you are using, who is still paying, and what processors are going to be the next big thing. Hopefully we can continue to make some dough here.

Comments or questions? What Autosurf programs do you use? What has been your experiences with autosurfing? I have been pulling in an average of about $1500 a month for the last 3 months from doing this. When my newer programs mature I will be making even more. I would love to hear about others experiences with this

Re: Autosurfing
You get paid a percentage of a membership level you are expected to purchase. Or you can surf on the money they give you for joining. The "front" is that you are paying to have a website you submit shown, and earning money for viewing a set number of other people's websites in the program (in a window that displays the sites sequentially like watching TV). In reality you are paying into a pool of money which is either invested, or added to other sources of revenue, and is then used to pay you.

These programs are like "moderately sustainable modified ponzi schemes". The programs rely on expansion for sustainabilty. In terms of investing these are very high risk, and you should only invest large if you follow whats going on in the industry - monitor who's investing in what, and who has the best track records. This is not a viable income alternative. Its better thought of as gambling with favorable odds.

The safer sites, like Paid Response and Studio Traffic have lower earnings, but will last longer. You can compound earnings for 3 months, and then you will get whatever you put in back for the next 9 months.

My first investment was Studio Traffic. I invested $100. With referral earnings My account is now at $540, or $5.40 per day. with referral earnings starting in september I will be pulling in $200+ monthly for at least the next 9 months (upgrades last one year) from an initial $100 investment.

 #108 
2005-09-12, 01:27
dagnabitt
Moderator
  
toronto
Re: Autosurfing
Compounding means to take what you earn in a given time and then reinvest it the program. 12daily does not have a compounding option, but most sites do. Compounding for a 1% site might look like this

100(account level)(m=month)

(m1)$100X.01%=$1(daily)x30(the month)=$30
(m2)$1 30x.01%=$1 .30(daily) x31=$40.30
(m3)$1 70x.01%=$1 .70(daily) x30=$50.10
(m4)$220x.01%=$2.20(daily)x30=$66.00
(m5)$280x.01%=$2.80(daily)x30=$84.00

So assuming no referrals, and that you put $90 into the program (with $10 upgrade) you will be making basically what you put in every month for around 8 months vs the $30 you would make if you just withdrew earnings every month. Tip for investing in
12Daily Risk Free

(or with greatly reduced risk)

Here's a tip for those that might be timid about investing in 12daily. Stormpay will refund your money up to $250 if the site goes down and does not pay you. It wont do this in all situations, but it should in the case of 12Daily. Why?

For starters, if you dont get what you pay for, even if there are no guarentees regarding payments, the site cannot continue to solicit funds without telling you they are not paying out. Thats fraud.

Now the reason this would work so well with 12Daily is that you are due your payment within 19 days of paying in. You are paying as well for a 30 day membership, renewed with each upgrade. If the site were to go down within 30 days of your upgrade you have not received what you paid for (your 30 day membership, and then would be enititled to a refund according to Stormpay's Customer Satisfaction policies. This is particularly true if the site were to go down within 19 days, because you were not even given a realistic chance to make any money by 12 daily's own rules. That is not what you paid for. Lack of Guarentee's aside you are buying at the very least the chance to make money. If you do not receive that chance then you are entitled to a refund because under these circumstances 12 daily did not deliver what you paid them for.

I have done this before with stormpay for another site where I paid for a 50 day membership, and the site went down within a few weeks. My money was refunded within 24 hours.

The reason that this doesnt work for all autosurfs is that stormpay has a 50 day limit within which time you need to file your claim. Many sites, such as 4 daily, require you to be a member at least this long to see any returns (particularly if you compound). So it would not be as simple in these cases.

Anyway, this is not foolproof, but in the case of 12Daily it is extra insurance that greatly increases the odds of success with an already amazing program.

First, decide what exchanger you want to use. If you're going to use AnyGoldNow, then you start by submitting a buy order at their site. They will then email you a request to fax them a copy of your phone bill (or something like that) as i.d. verification. Once they have that, they will email you instructions for the bank wire, assuming you're doing the wire. Then you go to your local bank branch and give them a copy of the wire instructions. When that hits, AGN they will transfer the funds into your e-gold account.

Oh, and for the record, the fees using e-gold are way cheaper when you receive payments from these hyip sites, and that is the most important. Fees are higher on the funding side, and it's definitely more of a hassle, but this will probably be your only wire.

Not only that, but so far 12dp is the only site I've seen that uses StormPay, while they all accept e-gold.

Re: Autosurfing
There are many people online that do that, but its REALLY risky. The thing with egold is that once its sent there is no getting it back. Paypal, on the other hand has all sorts of refunding capability. Plus its against paypal's rules to buy egold.

So the scam goes something like this

1) Exchange paypal for egold
2) User 1 sends paypal first
3) User 2 sends egold
4) User 2 then turns around and says user 1 ripped him off.
Paypal then reverses the payment, because the seller cant prove otherwise.

In short its just too damn risky.

Well unified, it's actually interesting how your initial investment is related to risk. If you invest a lot at once, there's the risk of the program going down, and you losing all of your cash. But if you invest a smaller amount, it takes longer for it to compound to reach your goal - obviously leaving your investment at risk for longer.

After spending quite a while playing with excel, it seems the best tactic for investing in the long haul is to reinvest 70% of your payout after the first time slot, and then 68% after the second, then 66% after the third, and so on.

Since you seem to be in this to make a quick buck, then it would probably be best to just invest it, and continually reinvest until you hit the 3,000 mark, which would happen after timeslot 4 (about 68 days) if you're funding with stormpay, or after timeslot 3 (about 51 days) if you're funding with e-gold.

Re: Autosurfing
I dont think the object of autosurfing is to "get in and out". I think the object is to get in in hopes of making money prior to the program going down. The idea is to make make more money than you lose. I really dont agree with these "predicitons" people make about autosurfs. These programs continue to defy peoples expectations on a regular basis. Programs expected to do well go down, others defy all odds and last for years, while all the while people act like experts and are frequently wrong. There are hallmark signs of a program in trouble, but noone can predict whats going to happen to a program thats doing good now many months down the road. There are simply too many unseen variables.

And just because they are ponzi's doesnt mean anything. People make money in Ponzi's. They will go down sometime and people will lose money, but studio traffic in particular has shown how the Ponzi model can be expanded upon to sustain itself for many years.

These programs are barely legal, they could be investing money in anything for all the user knows. The fact is there are too many examples of programs defying the odds to assume there is a science of prediction here. All you can do is go with your gut, and the hype, and place your bets.

Re: Autosurfing
Egold essentitally trades by weight. This way people can trade it from any country without worrying about exchange rates etc...

Its used for these programs ( as well as forex trading and other online ventures) because its highly liquid and does not do chargebacks. Egold can be inconvenient because you need to buy it through a 3rd party, but as soon as you get going with it its a far superior way to operate - especially if you keep your money moving.

Uniclear is at the moment the best way to buy egold. They dont take credit cards at the moment, and to be honest you will pay through the roof to use one anywhere, probably 10% up, and you will need to go through a verification process in order to do it.

You can try http://www.anygoldnow.com/, which is reputable. They allow you to buy gold through Emo, which you will need to verify an account for.

Policy Update
31-Jan-2006 14:40
Due to high volumes of fraudulent transactions made to merchants with commission based business models, StormPay can no longer process payments for those type of merchants who choose to accept more than one payment processing solution.

Using more than one payment processor is exactly the situation that �fraud� seeks out. This enables the fraudulent user to set up a fake profile with either of the processors, make a purchase or join the program, and then withdraw their earnings to the other processor where the real identity is used. This sort of activity makes it nearly impossible for either processor, or law enforcement to properly handle the fraud because the �trail� comes to an end. This is the cause for a great many chargebacks to those merchants which can be avoided.

As of 1/30/2006 StormPay must require Merchants with a commissioned based business model who choose to accept StormPay, to only accept StormPay. This is from their knowledge base

quote:
How do I certify my account?
Your account status can be viewed on the "Account Overview" page from within your account. When making purchases, the status of the merchant is available on the online form to submit payment. These account statuses are available for your protection. Please use the status to help make a decision concerning your purchase or receipt of funds. To obtain the status of a sender of funds, log into your accounts history and click on the transaction ID #. The status of the sender is available there.

Your account can have four status levels as defined below:

Unverified:
Unverified status means that your account has not been verified. Accounts with Unverified status may experience delays in receiving withdrawals. Accounts with Unverified status will have some restrictions on the amount that can be spent from a Credit Card and US Checking account (if applicable), within any given 30 day period. Unverified accounts may deposit up to $500 with a credit card, or $500.00 with a checking account per rolling* 30 days.

*NOTE* - All accounts that are NOT at Certified, or NetIBA Certified status are imposed a 5 day wait period on withdrawals of funds sent to their account. Read below on how to change your status to NetIBA Certified.

Phone Verified:
A Phone Verified account has been phoned by a member of the StormPay Inc. Verification Team and the owner of the card/checking account is aware of the charges spent to StormPay Inc. Phone Verified accounts may deposit up to $2000.00 with a credit card, or $10,000 with a checking account per rolling* 30 days.

Certified:
Certified accounts are accounts that have had successful funding transactions older than 100 days without any types of transactional problems. Accounts that are of �Certified� status are established StormPay members with good payment histories. Certified accounts may deposit up to $2,000.00 with a credit card, or $10,000 with a checking account per rolling* 30 days.

NetIBA Certified:
NetIBA ( www.netiba.com ) certification is the preferred method for account certification. NetIBA is a third party verification service who verifies the identity behind e-mail addresses, auction usernames, and website domain names. StormPay members who are NetIBA Certified have completed NetIBA�s simple, yet thorough, identity screening process. NetIBA provides a place in their registration application to inform them that you are a StormPay member. Once certification is completed at NetIBA, NetIBA will contact StormPay to upgrade your account status. If NetIBA certified prior to obtaining a StormPay account, please contact us to include your StormPay account ID and NetIBA certification number by selecting the "contact us" link at the bottom of the page. Visit NetIBA at http://www.NetIBA.com NetIBA Certified accounts may deposit up to $2,000.00 with a credit card, or $10,000 with a checking account per rolling* 30 days.

*Rolling 30 day periods. Example: An unverified account might deposit $250 on the first of the month. Then, on the 15th, they may deposit another $250 which meets the rolling 30 day limit. The first transaction of $250 will expire allowing another $250 on the 1st of the following month. Verified/Certified status does not guarantee in any way the legitimacy of the account holder or the product/services being purchased/sold. Please always use your best judgment when making purchases on the Internet as per our user agreement. Any account that is NOT at "Certified" status, will have a 5 day wait period to withdraw funds from their StormPay account.

quote:
Dear StormPay Member,

Please read this news update as it contains important information concerning your StormPay account as well as spends from your account to the "Auto-Surf" industry.

Traditionally "auto-surf" is a "traffic exchange" industry as to where persons gain traffic credits for promoting their URL (website address) in exchange for viewing websites offered by others. Any monies taken in on these types of "traffic exchanges" are normally for upgrades to have your URL (website) shown at a higher rate of exposure. For an example of how a true auto-surf works, you can visit www.autohits.dk or other sites comparable.

"Paid to click", or "Paid to Read" types of sites are normally where an advertiser pays to have his/her ad displayed and the end user gets paid a portion of the advertiser dollars for clicking on and reading/viewing the ad. The end user who is being paid for reading/viewing the advertisement does not spend any monies to participate. An example of this type of service is StormPay's own "StormClix" where participants are not charged to view advertisements and are rewarded an account credit for viewing the advertisement.

It has recently been brought to the attention of StormPay Inc. that the current rash of new Auto-Surf and Paid to Read accounts are NOT operating in the traditional manner. Further investigation by both StormPay and other outside investigational organizations/law enforcement agencies have have drawn early conclusions that these types of programs are nothing more than well hidden "Ponzi" or "Pyramid" schemes. While many of you may not agree, or wish to agree that these programs or illegally operated ponzi's, there are many facts that that are unavailable to you, or that may have been hidden by the operators of these programs. Please note that StormPay's user agreement has always banned merchant accounts for these types of activities.

Throughout the investigations into these programs, StormPay has asked the "Merchant(s)" to provide a detailed explanation of the workings of these programs including how profit margins and customer payments are made. These questions were asked point blank by StormPay while on a conference call with the owner/operator and their attorney. The requests for information from the "merchant" were simply denied leaving StormPay no choice other than to report those findings to the other organizations who required the information from StormPay. These findings and reports caused the seizure of funds of the merchant(s) StormPay accounts until all legal matters are resolved. Please be reminded that this could have been avoided if the merchant(s) could have, or would have provided information proving no illegal pyramid or ponzi activity.

Furthermore, investigations and calculations show that these merchants were already at an "upside down" point where they are/were not able to meet the financial obligations made to their program participants. These merchants who were already failing to make good on their claims seem to now be using StormPay as their "Scape Goat" for the failure of their own pyramid or ponzi scheme. These programs are always doomed to failure and for that very reason, deemed illegal. Please site the following from StormPay's user agreement:

"17. Get Rich Quick" Schemes: Get Rich Quick Schemes are prohibited resell items by StormPay. Get Rich Quick schemes include any type of self-employment, start-up businesses, or investment opportunity where the claims of profit or returns on investment are unrealistic or unsupported. By law, if a business opportunity costs $500.00 USD or more, the promoter is required to support any claims regarding earnings or profits with written documentation.

Pyramids don't pay. StormPay Inc. and the Federal Trade Commission caution consumers about clubs or programs that promise quick money for recruiting new members. Don't bank on the pyramid promise that someone else will pay you. For more information on get-rich-quick schemes, visit the FTC at www.ftc.gov.

We know that the most prominent question in your mind is "What happens to the money I sent these programs?" Please be aware if determination is made that these are ponzi schemes, a great deal of the funds received by these merchant's will have been used to pay obligations to those who joined earlier into the programs. In other words, they will have used your money to pay other members thus creating a deficit of funds needed to refund all users. Please be patient while investigators decide the best procedures for handling this serious situation. Contacting your credit issuers or banks requesting chargebacks only compounds the problems for all involved, including the merch!
ants and their customers, and delays returns of any funds. These actions could also be punishable by law.

I have been autosurfing for about 10 months now and am completely hooked. The general idea, for those who dont know is that you sign up for a program you feel good about (see below). You then pay an amount of money you feel comfortable spending into the program (or surf on any free units the site may give). In return you view other members websites in an "autosurf" window in order to make cash. After viewing a set amount of sites, you are paid a percentage of your membership level. You make money because your upgrade will be active long enough for you to make all your money back, and then begin to profit. You can also compound your earnings and earn even more.
